goal: Give a swallowed Import consent analytics emission a durable, routable Sentry signal — a guarded captureMessage at level 'warning' tagged subsystem:import_consent_analytics — alongside the structured warn it already emits, without making observability able to poison the caller's transaction.
non_goals: Any change to emitConsentEvent's savepoint, its catch narrowing (errorStringProperty(error,'code')), or which error classes are swallowed vs rethrown — #679 round 2 fixed that and it is out of scope
A HealthAlertPoller counter or any aggregation of repeated drift (option B on #697, deliberately declined: these are one-shot per-business events and Sentry already groups them)
#695's durable policy-block reason for the consent guard — a different sink with an open architectural question; the two are NOT designed together (owner decision 2026-08-08)
Any change to the two analytics event names, their keys, migration 102, or the analytics_events CHECK constraint
Widening reportCaughtError's interface to carry a level or extra tags for one caller
Configuring the Sentry alert rule itself — that is an ops action; this change only adds the runbook checklist item that names the tag to route on
user_visible_behavior: No owner-visible behavior change. The only observable difference is operational: a failed Import offer / Import decision analytics emission now mints a Sentry issue 'Import consent analytics emission failed' at level 'warning' tagged subsystem=import_consent_analytics and event_name=<the event>, in whichever lane the emission ran (Next server via instrumentation.ts, worker via worker/sentry.ts).
The existing structured warn line on stdout is retained verbatim — this is an additional sink, not a replacement.
invariants: Observability must never poison the success path (CLAUDE.md): the captureMessage is wrapped in its own try/catch, so a Sentry failure can never resurface into the caller's transaction. This is the property that keeps the #679 connect outage closed.
The savepoint stays one-directional: a failed emission still rolls back only itself; a caller abort still takes the event with it.
Only errors carrying a string `code` are swallowed; a code-less error (a handle without .savepoint) still rethrows, and reports nothing to Sentry on its way out.
No review text, tokens, handles, or event properties reach Sentry — only business_id, event_name, and the error message, the same fields the warn already carries.
src/lib/** domain modules receive their DB client as a parameter (invariant #15) — unchanged here; emitConsentEvent already takes tx.
edge_cases: Sentry uninitialized (local dev, preview without SENTRY_DSN): captureMessage is an inert no-op and must not throw or change the swallow behavior.
Sentry.captureMessage itself throws (transport/serializer failure): swallowed by the inner catch; the warn still emits and the caller's transaction stays usable.
A code-less emission failure (mockTx or a Sql-shaped handle without .savepoint): rethrown BEFORE any Sentry call, so a wiring bug is not laundered into a drift alert.

A connection-lifecycle error (CONNECTION_CLOSED, ECONNREFUSED) carries a string code and is therefore swallowed and reported — a known imprecision in the signal, documented on #697; it cannot manufacture a quiet success because a lost connection independently rejects the enclosing begin.

Both writers must report: createImportOffer's import_offer_created and recordImportDecisionAndEnqueue's import_decision_recorded run through the same emitConsentEvent, so one implementation covers both, but both are pinned by their own test.

rollback_plan: Not db_touching and not flag-gated: revert the single commit. The change is additive observability inside one catch block — no schema, no env var, no flag, no contract change. A partial revert is never needed.
observability: A Sentry issue titled 'Import consent analytics emission failed', level 'warning', tags subsystem=import_consent_analytics and event_name=import_offer_created|import_decision_recorded, extra carrying business_id and the error message — this IS the deliverable.
The pre-existing stdout warn line ('[import-consent] Import consent analytics emission failed') is retained, so Railway/Vercel log search stays a second, independent read.
